deep.reconstruction:
The page works out a combinatorial model of the 4-holed sphere and of its moduli space M_{0,4}. That space is the labelled λ-line, acted on by S_4 through S_4 → S_J ≅ S_3, where J is the 3-element set of partitions of the 4 holes I into two pairs. The previous page is headed M_{0,4}, M_{1,1}.

(1) Line 1 describes a map on the sphere drawn as a tetrahedron with truncated vertices; the truncations are the 4 holes. Each of the 4 triangular faces is cut into one central hexagon and 6 small triangles. The vertices are:
- the 4 tetrahedron vertices (valence 6),
- the 6 edge midpoints (valence 6),
- 3 interior points per face (valence 3), so 12 in all.
The faces are 24 triangles and 4 hexagons. The counts are s0 = 4+6+4·3 = 22, s1 = 12+4·9 = 48 (6 split edges plus 9 interior edges per face) and s2 = 4·7 = 28. The Euler characteristic is 22−48+28 = 2, as it must be for a sphere. The marginal note says this is better seen 'on the verso' as a barycentric subdivision. The next page adds that this map contains the barycentric subdivisions of the three associated 'cube' maps and of the passage cube ↔ two tetrahedra.

(2) The pencil sphere is the λ-sphere M̄_{0,4} with its symmetry group.
- Poles: the 2 equianharmonic (tetrahedral) points.
- Equator: the 3 cusps, drawn as holes, alternating with the 3 harmonic (square) points.
- A red-shaded sector serves as fundamental domain.

(3) There are '4 types of base points'. These are special configurations of the 4 holes on the sphere, given with the symmetry group that labels them.
- 3 square structures, one for each element of J, labelled S_J.
- 2 tetrahedral structures. These correspond to the two cyclic orientations, with ω_I = ω_J; the A_4/V_4 ≅ Z/3 orientation of I is the same as an orientation of J.
- 6 'bi-pantalonesque opposite' structures, identified with frames (orderings) of J, rep(J).
- 6 'pantalonesque' structures, identified with J × {orientation}, i.e. square + orientation, again ≅ rep(J).
The last two types are tangential base points at the 3 cusps: 4 per cusp circle, giving 12.

(4) There are '4 types of elementary paths'; the counts include both directions.
- a) quarter twist, 2×3×4: arcs of the cusp circles.
- b) sixth of a turn, 2×2×3: equatorial arcs between a cusp and a harmonic point.
- c) pole to hole, 2×2×3.
- d) pole to equator, 2×2×3: from an equianharmonic point to a harmonic point.
Composite paths:
- e) hole to hole, 'third of a turn', 2×3.
- f) half twist.
- g) full twist.
The page ends with 'relations…'.

(5) The bottom figure is a truncated tetrahedron with green midsections. It shows at once the passage from the tetrahedral configuration to the square configuration and to the pants configuration. The midsection of a regular tetrahedron parallel to two opposite edges is a square. When the two opposite edges shrink, the square becomes the pants curve separating the corresponding pair.

(6) The footnote says that with both directions there are 8 types of deformation to visualise, conformally and combinatorially.

Purpose: to obtain an explicit cell structure and presentation of the fundamental groupoid of M_{0,4} (with its S_4 / D_6-symmetry). The base points are tangential points at the cusps together with the orbifold points of order 2 and 3. This is the M_{0,4} building block of the 'Lego–Teichmüller' tower and of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller relations described in Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: No arithmetic error: 22−48+28 = 2. The overwritten digits (4.3 → 4·3; 4.9 = 48) are corrected on the page itself.

Consistency check of the path model: 17 base points (3+2+6+6) and 30 unoriented elementary edges (12 from a; 6 each from b, c, d). For the sphere minus 3 discs (χ = −1) this forces 12 faces. These are exactly the 12 fundamental domains of the extended S_3 action, i.e. of PGL_2(Z)/Γ(2) = D_6 on the λ-sphere. So the counts are coherent.
The '2^9 − 1 = 511' note is unclear. Its link to 'invariant positions of the chosen points' cannot be verified from the image.

ideas.what: Cell decomposition of the tetrahedrally symmetric 4-pointed sphere: truncated tetrahedron with each face cut into a hexagon plus 6 triangles (22/48/28 cells). It refines the tetrahedron map and the three 'cube' maps simultaneously.
ideas.modern_name: Regular maps / dessins d'enfants attached to the special points of M_{0,4}; common refinement via barycentric subdivision
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses regular maps and the tetrahedron/cube, but not this specific subdivision

ideas.what: Base points of the fundamental groupoid of M_{0,4}: tangential base points at the 3 cusps (pants decompositions, 12 in total) plus the 3 harmonic (square) and 2 equianharmonic (tetrahedral) orbifold points. Each type is identified with S_4/V_4 ≅ S_J-data: S_J, orientation ω_I = ω_J, frames rep(J), J × orientation.
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid with tangential and orbifold base points; λ-line with j = 1728 and j = 0 points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); tangential base points: Deligne 1989; developed by Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §2–3 (Teichmüller tower, M_{0,4}, M_{1,1}, 'points-base' and special points)

ideas.what: Elementary paths: quarter, half and full twists around the cusp circles; sixth and third of a turn along the real equator; pole-to-hole and pole-to-equator paths. These are generators of the Teichmüller groupoid of genus 0 with 4 holes, with relations to follow.
ideas.modern_name: Lego/Teichmüller groupoid generators (Dehn half-twists, braiding, associativity moves); 2- and 3-cycle relations of GT
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Lego-Teichmüller game, sketch only)

ideas.what: The tetrahedral → square → pants degeneration seen on one figure. The square midsection of a regular tetrahedron becomes the separating pants curve as opposite edges shrink.
ideas.modern_name: Paths in M_{0,4} from the equianharmonic point to the harmonic point to a cusp (real/rational slices)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a presentation of the orbifold fundamental groupoid of M_{0,[4]} that uses the orbifold points of order 2 and 3 as base points alongside tangential base points. He lists the elementary paths with explicit multiplicities but stops at 'relations…'. The later literature (Lochak–Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps) uses mostly tangential base points, so a groupoid version with orbifold base points is less standard.
missed.quote: 4 types de points-base … 4 types de chemins élémentaires … relations …
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Orbifold base points interact with the torsion elements of order 2 and 3 in GT-type groups. A presentation with these base points could give a symmetric derivation of the 2- and 3-cycle relations of Ĝ_T. This is mild interest only; most of it is implicit in known work.

missed.claim: The page explicitly plans to compare a conformal viewpoint with combinatorial ones ('deux pts de vue possibles') for the 8 deformation types. This anticipates comparing hyperbolic/conformal structures with map/ribbon-graph cell structures of moduli space, which Penner, Harer and Kontsevich later developed.
missed.quote: huit types de déformations à visualiser a) du pt de vue conforme b) du pt de vue combinatoire
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical evidence of Grothendieck's 1983 thinking on combinatorial cell decompositions of moduli space. It is not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, internally consistent worked example of the M_{0,4} building block of the Teichmüller tower. The base points and paths are counted equivariantly under S_J, and the orbifold points are included. It matches and slightly details what Esquisse sketches. No finished result absent from the literature is visible.
transcription_corrections: 'structures cavries/cavrée/cavré' should read 'structures carrées / carrée / carré' (square structures).
'4 sommets d'ordre 6 + 6 sommets d'ordre 6 + 12 sommets d'ordre 3' is correct. The second term is overwritten on '+4' in the image.
Top right marginal: likely 'mieux cf verso (subdivision barycentrique)'.
'$J \times \mathfrak{S}_J$' for the pantalonesque type is likely 'J × 2S_J' or 'J × orientations'; the count 6 = 3 × 2.
'bi-pantalonesques opposées' (with 'bi' inserted above the line). The parenthesis reads roughly '(maillot ceinturé)' and '(carrée + 2 diagonales) ≃ repère de J'.
'pôle vers équateur' is legible in the image for item d).
Left margin text: 'sur cette figure, on voit à la fois le passage du tétraèdre à la configuration carrée, et à la configuration pantalonesque des quatre [?] gants'.
